classification.difficultyReason: Apply the supplied definition of a polyhedron to distinguish flat polygonal faces from curved surfaces and solids pierced by holes.

content.prompt: Determine which of the following shapes are polyhedra.

spec.description: Elongated polygon-faced solid with a horizontal front upper edge, sloping lower edge, rear depth edges and two front right-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: Closed solid with only flat polygonal faces and no holes.
spec.answerVisibility: Question figure only; classification is hidden.

answer.worked: All its faces are flat polygons, and the solid has no holes, so it is a polyhedron.

spec.description: Inverted cone with complete elliptical top rim, marked centre and dashed axial segment from the front rim to the apex.
spec.mathematics: Cone with a curved lateral surface.

answer.worked: The cone has a curved surface, so its surface is not made wholly of flat polygonal faces.

spec.description: Hemispherical dome with a complete elliptical base and marked base centre.

answer.worked: The hemisphere has a curved surface, so it is not a polyhedron.

spec.description: Tall rectangular block pierced by two vertically stacked rectangular openings; top and right exterior faces and internal dashed depth edges are retained.

answer.worked: The solid is pierced by holes, so it does not satisfy the definition of a polyhedron used here.

spec.description: Extruded L-shaped solid with a tall left arm, lower right arm, uniform depth and dashed hidden rear edges.
spec.mathematics: Closed non-convex solid with flat polygonal faces and no through-hole.

answer.worked: All its faces are flat polygons, and it has no holes, so the L-shaped solid is a polyhedron.

spec.description: Cylinder rising to the right, with a complete near end, visible far-end arc and dashed hidden far-end arc.
spec.mathematics: Cylinder with a curved lateral surface.

answer.worked: The cylinder has a curved surface, so it is not made wholly of flat polygonal faces.
